name: Fahrenheit to Celsius Conversion
description: Construct a program that computes the Celsius equivalent of an input Fahrenheit value using the formula C = (F - 32) (5/9). The input Fahrenheit value is an integer.

comments.content: The constant BASE in the conversion formula, we set it to 32. We define BASE as constant because 32 is a constant in the conversion formula.

Note that constants hold a particular value for the duration of their existence and their value cannot be changed after initialization. By convention, uppercase letters are used when naming constants.

The constant CONVERSION_FACTOR, we set it to 5.0/9. We define it as constant because this factor is a constant in the conversion formula. Note that at least one operand of the division operator must be a floating-point number to ensure that the fractional part of the number is kept.

Note that constants hold a particular value for the duration of their existence and their value cannot be changed after initialization. By convention, uppercase letters are used when naming constants.
We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the Fahrenheit value.
We need to read the Fahrenheit value that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the Fahrenheit value by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

To get a Celsius equivalent of a Fahrenheit value, we subtract 32 from the Celsius value and multiply that by 5.0/9 (0.56). Note that the precedence rules dictate that the multiplication happens before the subtraction in the final conversion computation. Therefore, to enforce the subtraction to be performed before multiplication, we must use parantheses in the formula.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Fahrenheit Temperature: " and the value of variable fahrenheitTemp. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the variable.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Celsius Equivalent: " and the value of variable celsiusTemp. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the variable.
